core_meaning.primary_meaning: Furat corresponds to the Arabic form فُرات and is glossed in this record as “Sweet, pure, refreshing water.” The record associates the form with root ف ر ت (f-r-t). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Furat corresponds to the Arabic form فُرات (Arabic root ف ر ت (f-r-t); فُرات (Furāt)). Its core sense is sweet, pure water. Furat (فُرات) is the Arabic name of the Euphrates, literally 'sweet, pure, refreshing water'. It was borne by companions of the Prophet (Furat bin Hayyan and others). The source gloss 'little river' is a loose rendering of the 'fresh water' sense. The source's 'Male/Female/Unisex' gender string was normalised.
